name: std_FormatPutStringNarrow
signature: void std_FormatPutStringNarrow(FormatStream* stream, const char* text, u32 precision)
summary: Writes a narrow (char) string into a printf-style format sink, honouring the field precision and updating the remaining-width and written-count fields; each byte is handed to the sink's putc callback.
evidence: Called by 0x100C3C's narrow path; body loops text[0..precision] and calls (*stream->putc)(byte, stream->cookie) inside 0x2FF71C/0x2FF748 (padding begin/end); stream layout matches the printf stream used by std_PrintfFormatInt (0x1003F8, N_001) and std_PrintfFormatFloat (0x300090, N_001).

name: std_PrintfFormatInt32
signature: void std_PrintfFormatInt32(FormatStream* stream, int conv, va_list* ap)
summary: Formats a 32-bit signed/unsigned decimal integer (%d/%u/i) for the printf core: extracts the value from the va_list, builds the sign/space/plus prefix, converts digits and emits them through the shared padding writer.
evidence: conv==0x75 ('u') takes the unsigned path via 0x2FF780 (va_arg), otherwise 0x2FF76A (signed divmod) with sign detection and prefixes at 0x1003B0/0x1003B4/0x1003B8/0x1003BC; calls 0x2FF798 for digit extraction and 0x2FF7C4 (padding/zero-fill writer). Sits immediately before std_PrintfFormatInt (0x1003F8, N_001) which is the 64-bit variant.

name: std_PrintfFormatHex64
signature: void std_PrintfFormatHex64(FormatStream* stream, int conv, u32 hi, u32 lo)
summary: Formats a 64-bit value as hexadecimal (%x/%X), building digits from the 64-bit hi:lo pair and emitting the selected '0x' prefix plus zero padding.
evidence: Nibble loop over arg3/arg4 with shifts (hi:lo 64-bit), digit table selected by the 0x800 flag (0x1004F0/0x100504), '0x' prefix added when conv==0x70 ('p'), then 0x2FF7C4. Same calling convention as std_PrintfFormatOctal64 (0x100E18).

name: std_PrintfFormatHexArg
signature: void std_PrintfFormatHexArg(FormatStream* stream, int conv, va_list* ap)
summary: va_arg wrapper for the hex formatter: fetches a 32-bit argument from the va_list and delegates to std_PrintfFormatHex64 with a zero high word.
evidence: Body is exactly `uVar1 = func_002FF780(*arg3, arg1); func_001004E0(arg1, arg2, uVar1, 0);` - va_arg helper 0x2FF780 (the same helper used for 'u' in 0x100354) plus the 64-bit hex formatter; mirrors std_PrintfFormatOctalArg (0x100E5C).

name: std_mbrlen
signature: int std_mbrlen(const char* s, int n, mbstate_t* ps)
summary: C89 mbrlen: measures how many bytes of a multibyte sequence are consumed, using the caller's mbstate and returning -2 for an incomplete sequence and -1 for an illegal one.
evidence: Tail-calls 0x10067C (mbrtowc) with pwc=NULL, i.e. func_0010067C(0,s,n,ps); handles the NULL-s default ('\0' one-byte sequence); both return codes -1/-2 are the C standard's (size_t)-1/-2 conventions.

name: std_mbrtowc
signature: int std_mbrtowc(u16* pwc, const char* s, int n, mbstate_t* ps)
summary: C99 mbrtowc: decodes one multibyte character into a wide character using the current locale's converter, returning the bytes consumed, 0 for a null character, -2 for an incomplete sequence and -1 (setting errno EILSEQ) for an invalid one.
evidence: Uses the locale hook 0x2FF9D0 (same converter the printf code uses) with the caller's mbstate; sets errno through 0x2FF9C4 ('*puVar2 = 4') on invalid input; signature (pwc,s,n,ps) and -1/-2 returns match the C standard; callers are std_mbrlen (0x100658) and the wide/multibyte printf paths.

name: std_wcsncat
signature: u16* std_wcsncat(u16* dest, const u16* src, int count)
summary: Wide-character strncat: finds the end of dest, appends at most count wide characters from src and terminates the result.
evidence: Body: scan dest for 0, copy up to count src elements, write terminating 0, return dest. Exact wcsncat semantics; sibling 0x100AD6 was named std_Utf16CompareN by N_032 so the UTF-16 vocabulary is already established.

name: std_FormatPutStringNarrowDispatch
summary: Chooses how to emit a narrow %s argument: if the stream is in byte mode it writes the bytes verbatim, otherwise it converts the multibyte text to wide characters first.
evidence: Checks stream+0x14 (wide-mode flag) and calls 0x1002F8 (byte writer) when 0 or 0x100D28 (multibyte-to-wide) otherwise, returns 1; identical dispatch shape to 0x100FB4 (maybe_std_FormatSinkPutString, N_037) which handles %ls.

name: std_FormatPutMultibyteAsWide
signature: void std_FormatPutMultibyteAsWide(FormatStream* stream, const char* text, int count)
summary: Emits a multibyte string to a wide-character sink: a first pass counts characters with mbrtowc (honouring precision in characters, not bytes) and a second pass converts and writes each wide character.
evidence: Two passes using 0x2FF9D0 (mbrtowc); decrements stream->f_18 by the character count, then calls the sink callback with u16 values and increments f_20; the stream flags at +0x1c hold the precision limit.

name: std_FormatPutStringWide
signature: void std_FormatPutStringWide(FormatStream* stream, const u16* text, u32 precision)
summary: Writes a wide (UTF-16) string into a wide printf sink, honouring precision and updating width/count fields; the mirror image of std_FormatPutStringNarrow.
evidence: Same structure as 0x1002F8 but indexed on u16 and calling the sink with each u16; called by 0x100FB4 when the stream is in wide mode.

name: std_PrintfFormatOctal64
signature: void std_PrintfFormatOctal64(FormatStream* stream, u32 conv, u32 hi, u32 lo)
summary: Formats a 64-bit value as octal (%o), including the alternate-form leading '0' and zero padding.
evidence: Three-bit digit loop over hi:lo (`arg3 & 7` + '0'), the 0x20 flag forces the leading zero and decrements the width field, then 0x2FF7C4; direct sibling of the hex formatter 0x1004E0.

name: std_PrintfFormatOctalArg
signature: void std_PrintfFormatOctalArg(FormatStream* stream, u32 conv, va_list* ap)
summary: va_arg wrapper for the octal formatter: fetches a 64-bit argument and splits it into high/low words for std_PrintfFormatOctal64.
evidence: Body: `uVar1 = func_002FF780(*arg3,arg1); func_00100E18(arg1,arg2,uVar1>>32,uVar1,0);` - 64-bit va_arg helper plus the octal formatter.

name: std_PrintfFormatSpecialFloat
signature: void std_PrintfFormatSpecialFloat(FormatStream* stream, u32 flags, int conv, int sign)
summary: Emits the three-character special float spellings (inf/INF/nan/NAN) for the printf core, adjusting the width by the sign character and honouring the uppercase flag.
evidence: Exactly three characters are written from one of the four 3-byte literals at 0x100F9C/0x100FA0/0x100FA4/0x100FA8, selected by conv<7 and the 0x800 uppercase flag; width field (stream+0x18) is reduced by 3 or 4; caller is std_PrintfFormatFloat (0x300090, N_001).

name: std_ParseInfNan
signature: int std_ParseInfNan(u32 lo, u32 hi, int* endpos, int* scanctx, int pos, u32 bits, int len, int ch)
summary: Recognises the textual 'inf', 'infinity' and 'nan(...)' forms in strtod and fills the result's float bits (infinity plus optional sign, or a quiet NaN with the parenthesised payload skipped).
evidence: Compares the current character against 'I'/'N' (mask 0xffffffdf) and expects 'nf'/'aN'; on success writes 0x7F800000-style exponent bits and 0x400000 quiet-NaN bit into the float union; sibling 0x101314 std_Strtod / 0x101100 std_StrtofCore (N_001) are its only logical callers.

name: maybe_std_Abort
summary: Tiny libc wrapper that tail-calls the fatal-exit routine at 0x100F04; most likely abort() or a terminate helper.
evidence: Body is a single tail call to 0x100F04, which has no readable C file; it sits in the newlib block immediately before std_isspace (0x100F10, N_037) and next to std_strtod, and has no callers (called through a table/atexit slot).

name: Engine_Initialize
summary: One-time engine bring-up: initialises the heap system (InitHeaps), then lazily creates and wires every global subsystem singleton (resource caches, renderer, sound, task pool, input) using the repeated 'init-flag + aligned size + allocate + construct' pattern.
evidence: No callers (called from the startup/init table), it is the only caller of InitHeaps (0x102EF8) besides itself, creates ~12 globals via func_00116AE0(size, tag) + ctor (0x103724, 0x104A38, 0x1052C8, 0x104ED8, 0x103594, 0x10293C...), and finally calls func_00107D00/0x102EC0; mode 'arm' with a 0xC78 body.

name: maybe_Os_InitTimeStrings
summary: Fills three fields of a small global record from a 0x300308 lookup and the two constant-string getters 0x105238/0x105280, offsetting one by +1.
evidence: Body: iVar1 = func_00300308(0,g_00102870); *(iVar1+4) = func_00105238(0)+1; iVar1->f_c = func_00105280(0); the getters return '&literal + constant offset' (see 0x105238/0x105280), so this seeds string/locale fields; no callers found.

name: Engine_InitializeSubsystems

evidence: Body is an argument-free call chain 0x107024 -> 0x1071AC -> 0x107544 -> 0x1075FC -> 0x10DA2C(0x1e) -> 0x107618(3) -> 0x107608(1); called from 0x101B74 (Engine_Initialize) right after the cache/cache-set construction.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateFrameTasks
summary: Per-frame service update: advances up to five timed fade records, services the pending-transfer list, releases finished transfer slots and, when arg2==0, drops bulk-transfer bits; called from the main loop.
evidence: Body decodes a 5-entry bitmask at self+0x1AB0 with (start,current,step,remaining) float tuples, calls 0x105584/0x105AFC/0x10967C/0x106280, and is called from 0x694E18 (main loop) together with 0x101B74/0x10411C/0x104204/0x104520; exact owning subsystem (Gfx vs Fs) not proven.

name: maybe_Engine_GetUpdateMode
summary: Returns 1 or 2 depending on the sign of the value produced by 0x107E9C, i.e. maps a status/flag to a two-valued mode.
evidence: Body: `iVar1 = func_00107E9C(); return (iVar1 >> 0x1f) + 1;` - the same (x>>31)+1 idiom used for handle/status normalisation elsewhere; no callers.

name: maybe_Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks
summary: Main-loop callback dispatcher: runs up to four registered callbacks from each of several global callback arrays (frame begin, render, frame end), guarded by the runtime-state checks 0x10D68C/0x10CC00.
evidence: Walks 4-entry {fn,arg} arrays rooted at g_00102EB0 (offsets 0, 9, 0x12, 0x1B entries), invoking each non-null callback; brackets them with 0x11383C, 0x117C58/0x117B78 (lock), 0x1095A4(1/0); called from 0x694E18 (main loop) and 0x101B74.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFramePeriod
summary: Stores a period/frame-duration value in two fields of the context and resets the two timing helpers.
evidence: Body writes arg1 to ctx+8 and ctx+0x14 and calls 0x107894(0)/0x107880(0); no callers (table slot), so the meaning of the value is inferred from the two mirrored writes.

name: maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields(FsChannel* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one transfer channel object: stores its heap/callback pointer, builds the linked-list head at +0xE104/+0xE118 and creates the asynchronous transfer primitive (0x10EAB0) with the channel's 0x2000-byte staging buffer.
evidence: Writes f_E114=arg2, func_00111CD8(&f_E118,0,arg3,arg4,arg4), f_E104=self+4, then 0x10EAB0(&f_E0F8, f_E114, 0x2000, 0x11, 0xFFFFFFFE); called once from Engine_Initialize (0x101B74) with the cache-set base at +0x334.

name: maybe_Fs_ChannelTable_Create
summary: Constructs a 255-entry channel/queue table: allocates the object, installs the table vtable, fills each 0x18-byte entry with the entry constructor and terminates the array.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Initialize
summary: Builds the whole streaming-resource cache: allocates per-category slot pools and buffers for every pack category (sound, cmn_cache, weapon, PL_256/400, F_/B_ motion, sound, model, UI) and registers them in the named-table at the end.

Slot pools come from 0x108624/0x108750/0x1086CC/0x1087F4 with sizes 0x80000/0x40000/0x64000/0x12C000/0xBC0000.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitDrawList
summary: Submits the accumulated draw/command list for the current frame: takes the renderer lock, releases the transfer list, and for every queued entry calls the renderer's slot-0x20 command with the frame constants.
evidence: Body: 0x10AF94(&local); 0x108F64(local); if g_001041F0 then for i in (self->f_54..f_58)/8 call (*(entry->vtable+0x20))(entry,0x3F,local_18,0x100,10); called from 0x101B74 and the main loop 0x694E18.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderContext
summary: Flushes the renderer and destroys the owned renderer object (virtual slot +4), clearing the pointer.
evidence: Body: 0x10AF94/0x1092A0 lock+flush, then if self->f_18 != 0 call (*(*f_18+4))() and set f_18=0; called from Engine_Initialize and the main-loop teardown path 0x694E18, symmetric with 0x10411C.

name: Fs_MountDefaultArchives
summary: Lazily mounts the built-in archives once: initialises the archive device, opens the system file handle, registers the default mounts (name,size) and aborts through 0x118924 on failure.
evidence: Guarded by g_001042A8; calls 0x106AC0, 0x10BDF8 (Os_AcquireSharedSession), 0x106A6C, 0x1074AC(g_001042B0,g_001042AC) (Os_CreateEvent with a literals pair), 0x107514; error path func_00118924(iVar2, 0x104298); mirrors 0x1042B4 which undoes it.

name: Fs_UnmountDefaultArchives
summary: Undoes Fs_MountDefaultArchives: closes the event/device handles and clears the mounted flag.
evidence: Guarded by g_001042FC; calls 0x107470(g_00104300) (Os_CheckHandleClosed), 0x106A38 (Os_CloseHandleIfOpen), error path 0x118924(...,0x1042EC), then clears *pcVar1; exact mirror of 0x104240.

name: maybe_Mem_ResizePageBlock
summary: Grows or shrinks a page-granular memory block: when the size shrinks it unmaps the tail pages, when it grows it maps new pages and remembers the new base/size.
evidence: Only acts when (arg1 & 0xFFF)==0, compares with the current size at g_0010450C[1], then calls 0x1053D0(base,0,len,1,0) to unmap or 0x1053D0(base,0,len,0x10003,3) to map; stores the new base/size back; no callers (vtable/table slot).

name: Fs_CacheSet_UpdateEntries
summary: Per-frame cache-set update: walks the entry lists, sorts them by the 0x84 priority byte, applies pending visibility transitions through the entry vtable (+0x10/+0x14), releases unloaded entries (+0xC/+0x28) and merges the done-list.
evidence: Uses intrusive lists at self+0xC (head self+0x30) and self+0x34; entry vtable slots +0xC/+0x10/+0x14/+0x28; entry byte +0x84 is the sort key and +0x85/+0x86 the visible/pending flags; calls 0x1235A4 (list splice) and 0x109600 (list clear); called from 0x101B74 and main loop 0x694E18.

name: Fs_CacheSet_BeginEvict
summary: Asks every currently loaded cache entry to prepare for eviction (entry vtable slot +0x18).
evidence: Iterates the list at set[0]/set[1] and calls (*(*entry+0x18))() when entry byte +0x85 is set; sibling trio 0x1048BC (+0x1C), 0x10490C (+0x20) with the same loop; called around the main-loop frame in 0x101B74/0x694E18.

name: Fs_CacheSet_ReleaseEntries
summary: Releases cache entries that are no longer visible: unloads them (vtable +0x14), clears the visible/pending bytes, destroys the object (+0xC) and frees it (+0x28) until the done-list is empty.
evidence: Loop terminates when the list cursor equals self->f_1C; unlinks via 0x109620/0x109658; calls slots +0x14/+0xC/+0x28 exactly like 0x104520; called from 0x101B74, 0x55AD28 and the main loop.

name: Fs_CacheSet_EndEvict
summary: Second eviction phase: calls entry vtable slot +0x1C on every loaded entry (commit/discard prepared evictions).
evidence: Same 3-line list walk as 0x1047B0 but slot +0x1C; part of the 0x1047B0/0x1048BC/0x10490C slot-0x18/0x1C/0x20 family.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Flush
summary: Third eviction phase: calls entry vtable slot +0x20 on every loaded entry (final flush of cached blocks).
evidence: Same list walk as 0x1047B0/0x1048BC but slot +0x20; the three functions are always called together from 0x104520 and the main loop.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Shutdown
summary: Destroys all remaining cache entries: unlinks each block from the free list, detaches its buffer, releases the underlying allocation (0x10F6CC) and empties the set.
evidence: Walks self->f_1C..f_14 list via 0x115358/0x115390, frees f_34 via 0x10F69C, detaches f_10 records with 0x10EC00/0x10EC14 (intrusive-tree unlink), then 0x10F6CC(entry); called from Engine_Initialize and main-loop teardown.

name: Gfx_Display_Initialize
signature: void Gfx_Display_Initialize(GfxDisplay* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Initialises the dual-screen display: allocates 2-3 framebuffer/wave buffers per screen, four 0x200x0x200 and 0x100x0x200 render targets, the GPU shared block and the frame-timing counters.
evidence: Allocates 3 buffers per i in 0..1 with sizes n*96000, n*0x12C00, n*96000 (n=2 or 3 from Gfx config), two 0x100000-byte target blocks with 0x100 sub-entries, then 0x10944C(&f_C4,0x200,0x200,...) x4, and finally (config<<0x12) bytes for f_1E4 with svc 0x28; called from 0x101B74 with the display singleton; the 400/0x140 screen constants appear in 0x109FB0.

name: Gfx_Display_Shutdown
summary: Releases everything Gfx_Display_Initialize allocated: the shared block, the six per-screen buffers, the two 0x100000 target buffers and the two mapped regions.
evidence: Frees f_1E4 (0x10F69C), then 3 pointers x 2 screens at self+4, then f_44/f_48 for 2 entries, then 0x10E66C(...,f_BC/f_C0); exact inverse of 0x104A38; called from Engine_Initialize and the main loop.

name: Gfx_Display_PresentFrame

summary: Frame presentation: waits for the vsync deadline, DMA-copies the finished framebuffer lines (0x400 stride x 0xF0 rows) to the visible buffer, then swaps the active buffer index.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitDefaultTexture

name: maybe_Gfx_InitDisplayDriver
summary: Brings up the graphics driver once: stores the runtime flag, reads the display timing values (0x106F04/0x107298), and when they indicate a usable display config registers the 0x3000-byte command buffer and sets the display mode 10.
evidence: Calls 0x106F04, 0x107298, 0x107328(g_00105040,0x3000), 0x10C574(0,10); sets *g_00105038=1 and returns 1; failure path checks the 64-bit result against g_0010503C; called from Engine_Initialize and 0x106BFC-adjacent init path.

name: maybe_Fs_SetTransferPriority
